newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks end up, hit new highs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks end up, hit new highs.

text.p: Australian shares swaggered to a higher close on Thursday, defying a wobbly Wall Street and hitting new highs in the afternoon session before easing back.
The All Ordinaries index reached a record high of 2,429.2, surpassing the previous record high of 2,426.5 reached on December 31, 1996.
However, the benchmark failed to break its record close of 2,424.6 and by 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT) was 8.2 points higher at 2,423.2.
March share price index futures were up two points at 2,442, an 18.8 point premium to the index.

"The market generally firmed in every sector except gold which is still struggling," said director of institutions at Ord Minnett, Eric Gale, adding that an upbeat attitude to base metals had helped the market consolidate its late 1996 gains.

"Sentiment has changed for the better for the base metals. We have had a rise in copper stocks but the copper price continued to go up despite that, and we've had a good snapback in nickel and aluminium," Gale said.
"The only laggard is gold at the present time and sentiment for it is appalling at the moment," he added.

Major corporate news of the day was CRA selling its controversial Century zinc project in north Queensland to major zinc producer, Pasminco, for A$345 million. Pasminco shares closed marginally lower at A$1.92 amid uncertainty over native title issues and possible capital raisings to fund the deal.
"I would say the market regards it as a reasonable deal for both sides," Gale said, noting the importance of Century ore to Pasminco's Budel smelter in the Netherlands.
"If you see Pasminco a little weaker, the market may have already put it in a cum-rights situation but it is only off a little," he said.

Major miner WMC continued its run from Wednesday as nickel prices held up and received a further boost when its 39.25 percent owned Alcoa Australia announced a 15 percent higher net profit of A$395 million for the 1996 calendar year.
The good news from the second tier oil companies continued with shares in Petroleum Securities leaping after it announced a new discovery in its U.S. oil and gas fields in the Gulf of Mexico.
In the industrials, CSR benefitted at the expense of Pioneer International as traders switched funds between the rival building materials groups.
